title: Inference economics sketch: latency vs unit cost (working)
content:
Purpose:
To gather a compact, shareable sketch of recent microbenchmarks comparing latency and per-token cost across a few representative model+quantization profiles and runtime policy knobs. This is a working artifact (notes to self + rough charts) intended for discussion with product and SRE next week.

High-level takeaway (rough):
- For short-turn prompts (<=64 tokens) single-request p95 is dominated by setup + kernel dispatch; batching gives limited returns unless concurrency is >8.
- For mid-length responses (128-512 tokens) batching + KV caching yields the biggest unit-cost wins; quantized 8-bit models keep latency close while cutting cost ~30-40% vs fp16.
- For long outputs (>1024 tokens) throughput optimizations (continuous batching + cache reuse) produce the largest token/sec improvements but require relaxed latency SLOs.

What we measured (method):
- Test harness: local cluster replica (prod-like conv), using the internal perf harness (ENG-3421).
- Hardware: 1 x A100-80GB (driver kernel set A), and a separate run on T4 for lower-cost reference.
- Models/variants:
  * llama2-13b (fp16)
  * llama2-13b (q4f16)
  * mpt-30b (fp16, small sample)
- Configs:
  * batch sizes: 1, 4, 8, 16 (continuous batching enabled for >1)
  * concurrency: 1..16 workers
  * kv-cache: cold vs warm (warm = same session, reuse KV)
- Metrics captured: p50, p95, p99 latency (ms), mean latency, tokens/sec, GPU UTIL, estimated cost-per-1M-tokens (USD) using current infra unit costs.

Representative numbers (aggregated, rounded):
Table: p95 latency (ms) and cost per 1M tokens (USD) for a 128-token generation target, A100

Model Variant      | Batch=1 | Batch=8 | p95(B1) | p95(B8) | cost/1M tok (B1) | cost/1M tok (B8)
-------------------|---------|---------|---------|---------|------------------|------------------
llama2-13b fp16    | 1.0x    | 0.9x    | 220 ms  | 180 ms  | $42              | $14              
llama2-13b q4f16   | 0.95x   | 0.8x    | 200 ms  | 160 ms  | $26              | $9               
mpt-30b fp16       | 1.6x    | 1.4x    | 360 ms  | 300 ms  | $68              | $25              

Notes on table: cost estimates include amortized GPU runtime + memory + storage & network overhead assumptions. They assume steady-state batching at the target batch size.

ASCII charts (p95 latency, 128-token target):
llama2-13b fp16 : [##############----------------] 220 ms
llama2-13b q4f16: [###########-------------------] 200 ms
mpt-30b fp16    : [#########################-----] 360 ms

Tokens/sec (throughput) rough (higher is better):
- llama2-13b fp16  batch=8 : 160 tok/s
- llama2-13b q4f16 batch=8 : 280 tok/s
- mpt-30b fp16      batch=8 : 120 tok/s

Cost-per-1M tokens (explain):
- Formula used: (GPU hourly cost / effective tokens/sec * 3600) scaled to 1M tokens, plus 10% infra overhead.
- Using current A100 cost assumptions: $3.2/hr effective for dedicated amortized bucket (internal unit price).

Quick micro-insights (why q4 helps):
- q4f16 reduces memory bandwidth pressure and lets larger batch windows fit in L2/CUDA cache, improving throughput more than raw ops reduction would suggest.
- Kernel dispatch overhead still dominates for batch=1; q4 yields smaller absolute latency drops but big cost gains when batching.

Cold vs warm KV cache (128 token target):
- Cold session p95 ~ +20-35% vs warm (depends on model memory layout).
- Warm cache on repeated sessions effectively reduces per-token attention compute for prefix and produces up to 2x effective tokens/sec in some traces.

Preliminary charts (text) for cost vs latency tradeoff (each point = model+policy):
Latency (ms) -> 100    150    200    250    300    350
Cost ($/1M)       -> 8     12     20     30     45     70
Points: q4-b8 -> (160,9), fp16-b1 -> (220,42), fp16-b8 -> (180,14), mpt30b-b8 -> (300,25)

Operational notes / caveats:
- These runs were single-A100. In multi-GPU/multi-instance routing, network/serialization overhead will change the knee points for batching.
- Scheduler latency (queueing) not included — we measured raw runtime only. For customer-facing SLOs we need to add scheduler p95 (see ENG-3570).
- Cost model uses internal pricing buckets; public cloud MSRP would change absolute numbers but relative ordering should hold.

Open questions / TODOs (for next week):
- Run same suite on Dedicated instance type (reserved pricing) and on a 4x A100 pod to see scaling in multi-GPU horizontal throughput.
- Add T4 runs to provide low-cost tail reference and collect GPU mem pressure traces (nvprof) for q4 vs fp16.
- Validate results with real workload traces (chatty short-turn vs long-form). Can we re-run 20k trace samples from production? (linked: ENG-2889).
- Small experiment: CPU-based tokenization + batching consolidation to reduce per-request setup for short prompts — measure delta.

Communication plan (who to show and when):
- Share this draft with product-hosted-api and eng-sre ahead of the latency SLO review (week of Mar 9).
- Prepare a 1-slide summary for the March All-Hands: choose 2 charts (cost vs latency and tokens/sec) and one clear bullet.

Appendix: quick raw-run notes (timestamps, harness commands)
- run id 2025-11-25-A100-llama13b-q4-B8: ./perf_harness --model llama2-13b --quant q4f16 --batch 8 --tokens 128
- GPU util artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/2025-11/llama13b-q4-b8/util.csv

Quick meeting notes (from 2026-02-28 sync):
- Priya: prioritize q4 profiling for Dedicated launch playbooks.
- Maya: make dashboard tiles for: p95 latency by model+quant, cost per 1M tokens, KV hit ratio.
- Jamal: check regression thresholds for quality-vs-quantization.

Unresolved: exact mapping from internal amortized GPU price to customer-facing per-token price (finance needs final feed). Asking finance contact (see FIN-PR-19).

Bottom line for product: q4f16 looks like the best immediate lever to reduce customer unit costs while keeping latency within acceptable bounds for most use cases. But we need more end-to-end SLO runs (scheduler+network) before hard recommendations.
